s: What do SHG members often lack, which makes it hard for them to scale up beyond linkage loans?
x: Members often lack individual CIBIL credit histories needed to scale up, and linkage loans are seen as too small for expansion.

s: Which State has a 36% share in SHG-bank linkage and is described as a leading State in this area?
x: Andhra Pradesh leads SHG-bank linkage with a stated share of 36%.

s: What is the full form of SERP?
o: Society for Empowerment of Rural Poor
State Employment and Rural Prosperity Mission
Society for Eradication of Rural Penury
Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty
x: SERP is the Society for Elimination of Rural Poverty, which runs Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham.

s: In which year was SERP in Andhra Pradesh registered?
x: SERP was registered in 2000; it was split into AP SERP and TG SERP after 2014.

s: In which year was DWCRA (Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas) launched?
x: DWCRA was launched in September 1982 with Centre:State funding of 75:25.

s: With whose support does SERP run Velugu (Indira Kranthi Patham) in Andhra Pradesh?
x: SERP runs Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham with World Bank support.

s: What was the recovery rate of SHG-bank linkage loans in Andhra Pradesh in 2024-25?
x: AP leads India in SHG-bank linkage, with a 36% national share and 99.66% recovery in 2024-25.

s: In what ratio was DWCRA funded by the Centre and the State?
x: DWCRA, launched in September 1982, was funded by the Centre and the State in the ratio 75:25.

s: What is Stree Nidhi in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Credit cooperative federation promoted with SHG federations
x: Stree Nidhi is a credit cooperative federation promoted with SHG federations.

s: What is the full form of MEPMA?
o: Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas
Municipal Employment and Poverty Management Authority
Mission for Economic Planning in Metropolitan Areas
Mission for Empowerment of Panchayats and Municipal Administration
x: MEPMA means Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas and serves urban SHGs.

s: Up to what amount is SHG bank linkage permitted under the MEPMA self-employment programme?
x: MEPMA permits SHG bank linkage up to Rs 20 lakh; individual loans range from Rs 50,000 to Rs 2 lakh and group loans up to Rs 10 lakh.

s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Stree Nidhi – Credit to SHG members
x: MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas) works with urban SHGs; SERP works in rural areas.

s: What is the range of individual loans to members under MEPMA?
x: MEPMA individual loans are Rs 50,000-2 lakh; group loans go up to Rs 10 lakh and SHG bank linkage up to Rs 20 lakh.

s: For whom is the Pattabhi Sitaramayya-Self Business Group (PS-SBG) scheme of Andhra Bank meant?
x: Andhra Bank launched PS-SBG to help rural women start their own businesses.

s: What is the main service provided by Stree Nidhi to SHG members in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Stree Nidhi is a credit cooperative federation that gives timely, affordable credit to SHG members.

s: Which organisation in Andhra Pradesh works with self-help groups of the urban poor in municipal areas?
x: MEPMA (Mission for Elimination of Poverty in Municipal Areas) handles urban SHGs; SERP works in rural areas.

s: By whom has NABARD been fully owned since 2019?
x: Since 2019 NABARD is fully owned by the Government of India; it is headquartered in Mumbai and started with Rs 100 crore.

s: In which year was the Kisan Credit Card, a NABARD model scheme based on the R.V. Gupta Committee, introduced?
x: The KCC was introduced in 1998 as a NABARD model scheme based on the R.V. Gupta Committee.

s: In which year was the NABARD Act passed?
x: The NABARD Act was passed in 1981 and NABARD was set up in 1982, the same year as the EXIM Bank.

s: On its establishment, NABARD took over the whole of which body, besides RBI's ACD and RPCC?
o: Small Industries Development Bank of India
x: NABARD took over RBI's Agricultural Credit Department and Rural Planning and Credit Cell and the whole of the ARDC.

s:
Consider the following statements about the chronology of rural credit institutions:
1. Regional Rural Banks (1975) came before NABARD (1982).
2. The SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (1992–93) came before NABARD.
3. The Kisan Credit Card (1998) came after the SHG–Bank Linkage Programme.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The order is RRBs (1975), NABARD (1982), SHG–Bank Linkage (1992–93) and KCC (1998), so statement 2 is wrong.

s: Where is the headquarters of NABARD?
x: NABARD, set up on 12 July 1982, has its headquarters in Mumbai.

s: On the recommendation of which committee was NABARD set up?
x: NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD).

s: When was the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) set up?
x: SIDBI, the principal institution for MSMEs, was set up on 2 April 1990.

s: With what initial capital did NABARD begin in 1982?
x: NABARD began with Rs 100 crore; Rs 2,000 crore was the starting corpus of RIDF.

s: Which of the following was set up in 1982, the same year as NABARD?
x: EXIM Bank was set up in 1982 like NABARD; SIDBI came in 1990 and RRBs in 1975.

s: Which of the following about the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) is NOT correct?
x: RIDF began in 1995–96 with an initial corpus of ₹2,000 crore, not ₹20,000 crore.

s: Under the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), rural drinking water supply falls under which category?
x: Rural drinking water is under the social sector; rural roads fall under rural connectivity and minor irrigation under agriculture and related sectors.

s: Which of the following NABARD funds is wrongly matched with its purpose?
o: LTIF – State share of ongoing PMKSY irrigation projects
Warehouse Infrastructure Fund – Rural infrastructure loans to States
x: The Warehouse Infrastructure Fund supports scientific storage and APMC facilities; rural infrastructure loans to States come from RIDF.

s: To which fund does money from the sale of Government shares (disinvestment) go?
x: Disinvestment proceeds go to the NIF, not to RIDF.

s: What was the initial corpus of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF), created in 1995-96?
x: RIDF began in 1995-96 with Rs 2,000 crore and is administered by NABARD; disinvestment proceeds go to the NIF, not RIDF.

s: Which programme was taken up in Andhra Pradesh with NABARD support for land development?
x: Indira Prabha was AP's land development programme supported by NABARD.

s: What was the purpose of the Indira Prabha programme in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Indira Prabha aimed at developing the lands of the poor with NABARD support.

s: How many lift irrigation schemes in Andhra Pradesh were modernised under RIDF in 2024-25 to stabilise 1.03 lakh acres?
x: In 2024-25, 68 lift irrigation schemes were modernised at Rs 74.22 crore to stabilise 1.03 lakh acres.

s: Which sector receives the largest share of RIDF loans to States?
x: Irrigation gets about 30% of RIDF loans, ahead of roads (26%) and the social sector (21%).

s: Into which bank was Andhra Bank, founded by Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Machilipatnam in 1923, merged in 2020?
x: Andhra Bank merged into Union Bank of India on 1 April 2020.

s:
Consider the following statements about Regional Rural Banks (RRBs):
1. RRBs were established on 2 October 1975.
2. Prathama Bank was the first RRB.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: RRBs began on 2 October 1975, and Prathama Bank (Moradabad) was the first RRB.

s: Which committee's 1991 report began banking-sector reforms in India?
x: The Narasimham Committee I (1991) launched banking reforms through its recommendations to admit new private banks and deregulate interest rates.

s: On whose recommendation were Regional Rural Banks set up?
x: RRBs (1975) came from the Narasimham Working Group; Sivaraman led to NABARD and R.V. Gupta to KCC.

s: Who founded Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam in 1923?
x: Andhra Bank was founded by Bhogaraju Pattabhi Sitaramayya at Machilipatnam in 1923.

s: Nationally, scheduled commercial banks provide about what share of formal farm credit?
x: Scheduled commercial banks provide over 70% of formal farm credit nationally.

s: The lack of which of the following mainly keeps tenant, tribal, women and oral-lessee farmers in Andhra Pradesh out of formal credit?
x: Formal lending generally requires land records, which many such farmers do not possess.

s: Which of the following is NOT an institutional source of agricultural finance for farmers in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Commercial banks, RRBs and PACS are institutional sources; informal moneylenders are not.

s: Which institutions mainly provide long-term agricultural credit in India's cooperative credit structure?
x: ARDBs (Agriculture and Rural Development Banks) provide long-term credit, whereas the PACS-DCCB-State Cooperative Bank chain mainly provides short-term credit.

s: What is the maximum period of a short-term agricultural loan?
x: Short-term loans run up to 1 year, with a maximum of 15 months; longer loans are medium- or long-term.

s: From which date were Andhra Pradesh's four RRBs merged into Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank under 'One State, One RRB'?
x: The four AP RRBs were amalgamated into Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank from 1 May 2025.

s: Which is the sponsor bank of Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank?
x: Union Bank of India sponsors the single AP RRB, Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank.

s: Which of the following was NOT among the RRBs merged into Andhra Pradesh Grameena Bank in 2025?
x: Prathama Bank (Moradabad) was India's first RRB; the four merged were Chaitanya Godavari, Andhra Pragathi, Saptagiri and AP Grameena Vikas Bank.

s: After the 'One State, One RRB' amalgamation, to how many did the number of RRBs in India fall from 43?
x: RRBs in India fell from 43 to 28.

s: Up to what amount were rabi crop loans covered at the 20 April 2021 payout of the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme?
x: The scheme covered rabi crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh for farmers who repaid on time, with the State bearing the interest.

s: At what interest rate are short-term crop loans up to Rs 3 lakh available to prompt repayers under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme?
x: Short-term crop loans up to Rs 3 lakh are available at 4% for prompt repayers.

s:
Consider the following statements about the revised Kisan Credit Card Directions issued by the RBI on 19 June 2026:
1. They apply to loans from 1 January 2027.
2. They raise the maximum KCC tenure to six years.
3. The earlier maximum KCC tenure was three years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The directions apply from 1 January 2027 and raise the maximum tenure to six years; the earlier maximum was five years, not three.

s: In 2024–25, the disbursement of farm credit in India was approximately what percentage of the target?
x: Farm credit disbursement was Rs 28.69 lakh crore against a target of Rs 27.50 lakh crore, amounting to 104 per cent of the target.

s:
Consider the following statements about the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme:
1. It covers crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh repaid on time.
2. The State Government pays the interest.
3. It gives loans up to Rs 3 lakh at 4%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: The scheme covers loans up to Rs 1 lakh repaid on time with the State paying interest; Rs 3 lakh at 4% is the central Modified Interest Subvention Scheme.

s: Who bears the interest on eligible loans under the YSR Zero Interest Crop Loan scheme?
x: The State pays the interest on crop loans up to Rs 1 lakh repaid on time.

s: Into which document are district Potential Linked Credit Plans aggregated?
x: District PLPs are aggregated into NABARD's State Focus Paper, which then feeds the SLBC Annual Credit Plan.

s: Andhra Pradesh's State Focus Paper for 2026-27 allocated how much to agriculture and allied activities?
x: The plan allocated Rs 2.55 lakh crore to agriculture and allied activities and Rs 1.64 lakh crore to MSMEs.

s: By what percentage did the Andhra Pradesh credit plan for 2022-23 raise agricultural credit?
x: The 2022-23 plan increased credit by 10%.

s: What total credit potential for Andhra Pradesh did NABARD's State Focus Paper 2026-27 estimate?
x: The SFP 2026-27, unveiled on 5 May 2026, estimated Rs 5.11 lakh crore; Rs 2.96 lakh crore is the ACP 2025-26 figure for agriculture and allied.

s: How much of Andhra Pradesh's SFP 2026-27 credit potential is for crop loans?
x: Crop loans are Rs 1.66 lakh crore of the Rs 2.55 lakh crore for agriculture and allied; Rs 1.64 lakh crore is for MSMEs.

s: AP's SLBC Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 allotted how much to agriculture and allied activities?
x: The ACP 2025-26 (January 2026) gave Rs 2.96 lakh crore to agriculture and allied; Rs 5.11 lakh crore is the SFP potential.

s: AP's Annual Credit Plan 2025-26 set aside how much for tenant farmers?
x: The ACP 2025-26 earmarked Rs 1,490 crore for tenant farmers.

s:
Consider the following statements about the 236th SLBC meeting of Andhra Pradesh (16 September 2026):
1. The Chief Minister said MSME lending was below expectations.
2. Banks were asked to lend for PM Surya Ghar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Both are correct: the CM noted weak MSME lending and asked banks to lend for PM Surya Ghar.

s: In Andhra Pradesh's credit-planning chain, which plan follows the NABARD State Focus Paper?
x: District PLPs feed the NABARD State Focus Paper, which in turn feeds the SLBC Annual Credit Plan.

s: By about what percentage is the credit potential in NABARD's State Focus Paper 2026-27 for Andhra Pradesh higher than the earlier Rs 4.24 lakh crore?
x: The SFP 2026-27 credit potential of Rs 5.11 lakh crore is about 20% above Rs 4.24 lakh crore.

s:
Consider the following statements about Rythu Bazars and price stabilisation in Andhra Pradesh:
1. They are the State's quickest market-intervention channel for perishable commodities.
2. Export prices of perishables are fixed through them by the Reserve Bank of India.
3. The Government procures perishables through them to stabilise prices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: For perishables, the Government intervenes through procurement in Rythu Bazars to stabilise prices; they have nothing to do with RBI-fixed export prices.

s: Each Rythu Bazar is managed by an Estate Officer and comes under which department?
x: A Rythu Bazar is managed by an Estate Officer and functions under the Revenue Department.

s: To whom do farmers sell their produce directly in a Rythu Bazar?
x: Farmers sell directly to consumers in Rythu Bazars, whereas in regulated market yards they sell to licensed traders.

s: Who coordinates the functioning of Rythu Bazars at the district level in Andhra Pradesh?
o: District Agricultural Trade and Marketing Officer
Estate Officer of the nearest market yard
x: The Joint Collector is the coordinating officer for Rythu Bazars. The District Collector is not the coordinating officer for this purpose.

s: Prices in Rythu Bazars are fixed at about what percentage above wholesale prices and below local retail prices?
x: Rythu Bazar prices are fixed with the aim of being around 25% in relation to open-market prices.

s: Outside the purview of which body do Rythu Bazars in Andhra Pradesh function?
x: Rythu Bazars are run by an Estate Officer under the Revenue Department and lie outside AMC purview.

s: How many Rythu Bazars were functioning in AP in 2025-26?
x: 129 Rythu Bazars functioned in 2025-26, up from 124 in 2024-25.

s: In which year did the Rythu Bazar scheme start in Andhra Pradesh?
x: The AP Government started Rythu Bazars in 1999; they have functioned from January 1999.

s:
Consider the following statements about Rythu Bazars in Andhra Pradesh:
1. They function outside the purview of Agricultural Market Committees.
2. They were set up under the AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: Rythu Bazars are an executive scheme of 1999 outside AMC purview; market yards, not Rythu Bazars, rest on the 1966 Act.

s:
Match the following:
List-I (Officer)
A. Estate Officer
B. Joint Collector
C. District Agricultural Trade and Marketing Officer
List-II (Role)
1. Supervises agricultural markets in the district
2. Manages a Rythu Bazar day to day

s: By what name was the farmers' market (Ryot Bazar) scheme first introduced in Punjab?
x: The Ryot Bazar idea came first in Punjab as Apni Mandi; Andhra Pradesh was the second State.

s: Which was the second State in India to implement the Ryot Bazar scheme?
x: After Punjab's Apni Mandi, Andhra Pradesh was the second State, with Rythu Bazars from 1999.

s: What was the corpus of the Price Stabilisation Fund in Andhra Pradesh's 2019-20 budget?
x: The Price Stabilisation (Market Intervention) Fund began with Rs 3,000 crore in 2019-20.

s: For intervention in which crops is Andhra Pradesh's Price Stabilisation Fund meant?
o: Foodgrains procured by the FCI only
x: The fund intervenes in agricultural and horticultural crops to secure a just price.

s: In 2019, farmers of which crop in seven AP districts were compensated from the Price Stabilisation Fund?
x: Groundnut farmers of seven districts were compensated from the fund in 2019.

s: In 2025-26, how many of Andhra Pradesh's 1,052 warehouse godowns were operational?
x: AP had 1,052 godowns (9.65 lakh MT); 643 were operational with 5.92 lakh MT capacity.

s: What is the main post-harvest infrastructure gap identified in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Limited operational storage and need for more cold storage
x: The main gap is limited operational storage, along with the need for more cold-storage facilities.

s: What does the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund primarily support?
o: Uniform MSP procurement of all crops
Farm-gate infrastructure at Rythu Bharosa Kendras
x: AIF funds farm-gate infrastructure at Rythu Bharosa Kendras and the conversion of PACS into multipurpose facility centres.

s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh State Warehousing Corporation set up?
x: APSWC was set up in August 1958 under the Warehousing Corporations Act.

s: In what ratio do GoAP and the Central Warehousing Corporation hold the share capital of APSWC?
x: APSWC's share capital is shared 50:50 between GoAP and CWC.

s: Under the Raitu Bandhu scheme in Andhra Pradesh, against what can farmers get loans?
o: Their produce pledged in market-yard godowns
x: Under Raitu Bandhu, a farmer pledges produce in market committee godowns and borrows on it, avoiding forced sales.

s: Which of the following is NOT a problem faced by farmers selling alone to traders?
x: Open auction is a remedy of the 1966 Markets Act; forced sales, false weights and unrecorded prices are the problems.

s: Andhra Pradesh addresses farmers' weak bargaining power in agricultural marketing mainly through which three mechanisms?
o: Rythu Bazars, cold stores and export zones
Regulated market yards, Rythu Bazars and e-NAM
x: AP answers the imbalance with regulated market yards (by law), Rythu Bazars (direct sale) and e-marketing (e-NAM).

s: The AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Rules, 1969 were framed under which provision?
x: The AP (AP&L) Markets Rules, 1969 were framed under Section 33 of the 1966 Act.

s: What happened to the 1966 Agricultural Market Committee framework after the three central farm laws were repealed in November 2021?
o: Was replaced by the Model APMC Act
x: The 2020 farm laws were repealed in November 2021, but the 1966 AMC framework remained operative.

s: Which of the following was a feature of the Model APMC Act?
x: The Model APMC Act introduced a single market fee, registration in place of licensing, and farmers' and consumers' markets.

s: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966?
o: Coverage of crops, livestock and livestock products
Abolition of all licensed buyers from market transactions
Use of standard weights and recording of prices
x: The Act provides for licensed buyers; it does not abolish them. It covers crops, livestock and livestock products and promotes open auctions, standard weights and recorded prices.

s: What is the Act number of the AP (Agricultural Produce and Livestock) Markets Act, 1966?
x: It is Act No. 16 of 1966; Section 33 is the provision under which the 1969 Rules were made.

s: Under the Model APMC Act, what replaces the licensing of traders?
x: The Model APMC Act provides registration in place of licensing and a single market fee.

s: Under the Andhra Pradesh framework, what is the first step in setting up a regulated market?
x: The Government first declares a notified area, then constitutes a Market Committee, which establishes the notified market.

s: Who supervises agricultural markets at the district level in Andhra Pradesh?
o: District Agricultural Trade and Marketing Officer
x: The DATMO supervises markets at district level; the Joint Collector coordinates Rythu Bazars.

s: Where is the second largest market yard in Andhra Pradesh?
x: Adoni market yard in Kurnool district is the second largest in AP.

s: What is the market fee in Andhra Pradesh's regulated market yards?
x: Regulated yards levy a market fee of 1%.

s: Which market yard in Andhra Pradesh is Asia's largest chilli market?
x: Guntur Mirchi Yard is Asia's largest chilli market; an Agri Export Zone for red chillies is proposed in Guntur.

s: How much market fee was collected in Andhra Pradesh's regulated markets in 2024-25 (up to December 2024)?
x: Market fee collected was Rs 433.39 crore in 2024-25 (to Dec 2024) and Rs 429.77 crore in 2025-26 (to Dec 2025).

s: For which crop is an Agri Export Zone proposed in Guntur?
x: Guntur Mirchi Yard is Asia's largest chilli market, and an Agri Export Zone for red chillies is proposed there.

s: What share of their income have Agricultural Market Committees in Andhra Pradesh paid into the Central Market Fund since October 2015?
x: The contribution was raised from 10% to 25% of income from October 2015.

s: Into which fund do the Agricultural Market Committees of Andhra Pradesh pay a share of their income?
x: Market Committees pay 25% of their income into the Central Market Fund.

s: In which area has e-NAM so far mainly helped agricultural marketing?
o: Fully enabling payments across all mandis
x: e-NAM facilitates price discovery but is not yet fully operational for payments or inter-mandi trade.

s:
Consider the following statements about e-NAM in Andhra Pradesh:
1. AP had 33 mandis on e-NAM in March 2026.
2. e-NAM is fully working for inter-mandi trade in AP.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: AP had 33 e-NAM mandis (22 in December 2019); e-NAM has mainly helped price discovery, not yet inter-mandi trade.

s: Besides free software, how much assistance did each Andhra Pradesh mandi integrated with e-NAM receive?
x: Each integrated mandi got free software and Rs 30 lakh assistance.

s: About how many mandis in 23 States and 4 Union Territories are linked to e-NAM?
x: e-NAM links 1,656 mandis in 23 States and 4 UTs; Andhra Pradesh has 33 of them.

s: How many FPOs in Andhra Pradesh are integrated with e-NAM?
x: 39 FPOs are on e-NAM in AP; 33 is the number of AP e-NAM mandis.

s: How many FPOs does the central scheme for Farmer Producer Organisations aim to form?
x: The central scheme targets 10,000 FPOs with a budget of Rs 6,860 crore.

s: What is the budget of the central scheme for 10,000 FPOs?
x: The 10,000-FPO scheme has a budget of Rs 6,860 crore.

s: Which of the following pairs (farmer's problem – channel) is correctly matched?
o: Forced sale right after harvest – Raitu Bandhu pledge loan
Small, scattered lots – Price Stabilisation Fund
x: Raitu Bandhu pledge loans prevent forced sales; middlemen margin is met by Rythu Bazars, scattered lots by FPOs, false weights by regulated yards.

s: Which of the following strategic sectors are being targeted by Andhra Pradesh for directing FDI?
o: AI infrastructure, critical minerals, semiconductors, energy transition and advanced technologies
Only conventional textiles, leather and tourism
Agriculture subsidies, public distribution and municipal services
Only coal mining and petroleum refining
x: The strategic FDI push covers AI infrastructure, critical minerals, semiconductors, energy transition and advanced technologies.

s: Manufacturing contributes approximately what share of the Gross State Domestic Product of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Manufacturing contributes about 11% of Andhra Pradesh's GSDP.

s: What is the weight of the revised core-industry index covering nine industries?
x: The revised nine-industry core index has a 32.88% weight; the earlier eight-industry index had 40.27%.

s: With technical collaboration from which country was the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant, dedicated to the nation on 1 August 1992, built?
x: The Visakhapatnam Steel Plant is a shore-based integrated steel plant built with Soviet (USSR) technical collaboration.

s: Cement production in Andhra Pradesh is concentrated mainly in which group of districts?
x: The principal concentration of cement industries is in YSR Kadapa, Kurnool and Guntur districts.

s: For which of the following is Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City at Parawada in Anakapalli a hub?
o: Bulk drugs and active pharmaceutical ingredients
x: Jawaharlal Nehru Pharma City at Parawada is a bulk-drug and API hub, with units of Hetero and Laurus.

s: Towards which type of industries did the MSME profile of Andhra Pradesh shift after bifurcation?
x: The post-bifurcation MSME profile of AP shifted towards capital-intensive industries.

s: What was Andhra Pradesh's rank among States in industrial output according to the RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States 2020-21?
x: The RBI Handbook 2020-21 placed AP 7th in industrial output (APPSC 2023). 13th is AP's rank in FDI inflows in January-December 2021; 3rd and 5th are not supported.

s: Which of the following district-sector pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nellore — Leather, electronics and auto components
Kadapa — Agro and food processing, chemicals and petrochemicals
x: Kadapa is associated with textiles, while Anantapur is associated with textiles and electronics. Agro and food processing, chemicals and petrochemicals are associated with Srikakulam.

s: Which of the following is NOT listed as one of the five major endowments of Andhra Pradesh?
o: A national surplus of coal reserves
A 974-km coastline described as the second-longest
x:
'974-km coastline, second-longest' — now 1,053.07 km, 3rd after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu (PIB Release 2198800 (4 Dec 2025, coastline revised to 11,098.81 km; AP 1,053.07 km, 3rd)).
A national surplus of coal is not one of AP's endowments; its strengths are the coastline, six operational ports, minerals, a farm base and surplus power (the coastline is now 1,053.07 km, 3rd longest, not '974 km, 2nd').

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about AP's industrial base?
o: AP has the longest coastline in India
x:
AP coastline 974 km, 2nd longest — now 1,053.07 km, 3rd after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu (PIB Release 2198800 (4 Dec 2025, coastline revised to 11,098.81 km; AP 1,053.07 km, 3rd)).
AP does not have the longest coastline: its coast is 1,053.07 km, 3rd after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu (revised 2025; earlier '974 km, 2nd'). Manufacturing about 11% of GSDP, 7th in industrial output and six operational ports are correct.

s: What type of integrated steel plant is the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant of RINL?
x: VSP is a shore-based integrated plant built with USSR collaboration.

s: Mangampet in YSR Kadapa is the world's single largest deposit of which mineral?
x: Mangampet holds the world's largest single barytes deposit.

s: Which organisation mines the Mangampet barytes deposit?
x: APMDC mines the Mangampet barytes.

s: Where did NGRI find traces of lithium and gallium in August 2026?
x: NGRI found lithium and gallium traces at Tummalapalle in Kadapa.

s: How many operational cement plants did Andhra Pradesh have in 2014-15?
x: AP had 26 operational cement plants in 2014-15, mainly in YSR Kadapa, Kurnool and Guntur.

s: According to APEDB, what share of India's exports did Andhra Pradesh contribute by 2020-21?
x: APEDB reported that AP contributed 5.8% of India's exports by 2020-21.

s: To which base year was India's Index of Industrial Production (IIP) revised in 2026?
x: In Jun-Jul 2026 the IIP base was revised to 2022-23 and the core index widened to nine industries.

s: Which industry was added when India's index of core industries was widened from eight to nine industries in 2026?
x: Iron ore was added, making nine core industries with a weight of 32.88%.

s: To what does Google's proposed investment in Andhra Pradesh relate?
o: A 1 GW AI data centre at Visakhapatnam–Anakapalli
A 2 MTPA steel plant at Kadapa
x: Google has announced a 1 GW AI data centre in the Visakhapatnam–Anakapalli region, involving an investment of US$15 billion or approximately ₹87,520 crore.

s: Which company is associated with an 8.2 MTPA steel plant proposed at Rajayyapeta/Nakkapalli in Anakapalli?
x: ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel is associated with the proposed 8.2 MTPA steel plant at Rajayyapeta/Nakkapalli in Anakapalli, involving investment of over ₹1.35 lakh crore.

It is a single Government-to-Business point for industrial clearances
It requires physical visits to regulators for every clearance

x: The portal was designed for 93 clearances from 19 departments within 21 days.

o: Andhra Pradesh Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002
Andhra Pradesh Ease of Doing Business Act, 2020

s: Under Andhra Pradesh's statutory single-window framework, what happens to an application not decided within the service-level deadline?
x: The Act provides for deemed approval when a department misses the prescribed deadline.

o: Providing one application point for every clearance required by an investment proposal
Providing only post-operation approvals to existing factories
Replacing all industrial licences with tax exemptions

o: AP Omnibus (Speed of Doing Business) Bill, 2026

o: AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002

o: AP Industrial Single Window Clearance Act, 2002

x: District Industries Centres implement the MSMED Act at the district level.

o: A one-stop resource and support centre for industries
A single-window portal for land registration only
An overseas investment facilitation centre at Busan

x: P4 denotes Public-Private-People Partnership.

x: The MSME Policy and the Single Desk Policy both belong to 2015-20; the Industrial Development Policy listed is the 2020-23 edition and IDP (4.0) covers 2024-29.

s: To what level does IDP (4.0) 2024-29 aim to raise manufacturing GVA from Rs 3.4 lakh crore in FY24?
x: The policy targets manufacturing GVA rising from Rs 3.4 lakh crore in FY24 to Rs 7.3 lakh crore.

s: How much investment does Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29 target?
x: IDP (4.0) targets Rs 30 lakh crore investment, US$10 billion FDI and five lakh manufacturing jobs.

Land acquisition through compulsory purchase alone

x: Textiles is a Sustenance sector, not a Propelling sector; aerospace and blue economy are Propelling and auto is Sustenance.

x: IDP (4.0) is G.O.Ms.68; the MSME policy is G.O.69, Electronics Manufacturing G.O.70 and Food Processing G.O.71.

o: Increase imports and restrict domestic manufacturing
Replace all private investment with public investment
Cut the cost of production and raise the speed of doing business
Maximise taxation and reduce industrial employment

x: G.O.Ms.71 is the Food Processing Policy (4.0); MSME is G.O.69.

x: IDP (4.0) lists 10 Sustenance and 10 Propelling sectors.

x: Blue economy is a Propelling sector; automobile, pharma and textiles are Sustenance sectors.

s: How many first-time manufacturing jobs does Andhra Pradesh's Industrial Development Policy (4.0) 2024-29 target?
x: IDP (4.0) aims at 5 lakh first-time manufacturing jobs.

x: IDP (4.0) targets 175+ industrial parks.

o: 10% of the Government of India PLI incentive, capped at 5% of FCI
5% of the Government of India PLI incentive, capped at 10% of FCI
15% of export turnover, capped at 5% of FCI
x: The PLI top-up is 10% of the Government of India incentive and is capped at 5% of FCI.

s: What mechanism was added in IDP 4.0 to ensure timely payment of promised subsidies?
x: IDP 4.0 introduced an Escrow Guarantee mechanism for timely payment of promised subsidies.

s: Pavala vaddi enables a unit to pay interest effectively at which rate per ₹100 per month?
x: Under pavala vaddi, the State reimburses interest above 3% a year, so the unit effectively pays a quarter rupee, or 25 paise, per ₹100 per month.

s: Under IDP (4.0), above what investment is a unit classified as Ultra Mega?
x: Ultra Mega units involve investment above Rs 5,000 crore and get a tailor-made package; the standard period is four years.

s: Under which category is a project involving investment of Rs 2,000 crore or generating 2,000 or more direct jobs classified?
x: A mega project involves ₹1,001–5,000 crore investment or 2,000 or more direct jobs.

s: To what is the local procurement subsidy under Industrial Development Policy (4.0) linked?
o: 1% of export turnover for three years
10% of export turnover for two years
5% of domestic turnover for three years
x: The local procurement subsidy is 1% of export turnover for three years.

s: The Employment Creation Subsidy for units with more than five employees is up to what share of FCI?
x: The subsidy is up to 10% of FCI for units with more than five employees (8–9% for five or fewer), paid over five years.

s: Under IDP (4.0), eligible units get reimbursement of what share of net SGST for five years from commercial production?
x: IDP (4.0) reimburses 100% of net SGST for five years on final products made, sold and registered in AP.

x: For medium, large and mega units, SGST reimbursement was tied to employment creation for five years.

s: Under IDP (4.0), to what is the investment subsidy restricted for a Large project that has installed only 50% of its capacity?
x: For a Large project with only 50% capacity installed, the subsidy is limited to 6%; otherwise the ceiling may be up to 12%.

s: What is the fixed power cost reimbursement under IDP (4.0)?
x: Fixed power cost is reimbursed at Rs 1 per unit for 2 years.

x: The State repays interest above 3% a year, so the unit pays 25 paise per Rs 100 per month.

x: AP's local employment Act of 2019 reserves 75% of industrial jobs for locals.

x: Large units get it in 7 instalments; Sub-Large units in 5.

x: APIIC gave a 25% land rebate up to Rs 20 lakh.

x: FCI is Fixed Capital Investment with land excluded.

s: Under the AP Industrial Development Policy 2020-23, for which group of entrepreneurs were 16.2% of APIIC plots reserved?
x: IDP 2020-23 reserved 16.2% of APIIC plots for SC entrepreneurs.

s: What is the full form of FCI in the context of Industrial Development Policy (4.0)?
x: FCI means Fixed Capital Investment.

o: A COVID-19 relief package for MSMEs
A policy for foreign direct investment in defence
A programme for constructing industrial corridors

s: Under AP's Food Processing Policy (4.0), what investment makes a unit Mega?

x: A small enterprise now has investment up to Rs 25 crore and turnover up to Rs 100 crore.

x: The policy envisages more than 175 MSME parks, with at least one park in each assembly constituency.

Financing only new steel plants in Rayalaseema

Emergency ambulance service for road accidents
Free drop-home for mothers and newborns after delivery in government hospitals

x: Five colleges opened in September 2023 as the first of 17 planned.
